insert into public.levels_preguntas (id, examen_id, level_id, parte_id, enunciado, creado_en) values (gen_random_uuid(), 'ae0e85e8-3d63-11f1-b2e3-0b27f7b23431', 'ae0e85e8-3d63-11f1-b2e3-0b27f7b23431', 'bd41d80c-bcdd-4ac9-9c06-13c2ab8fab6e', 'Text\nPart 7: Multiple Matching
You are going to read an article in which four people talk about their experiences of learning new skills. For questions 37–42, choose from the people (A–D). The people may be chosen more than once.

Which person…
37 mentions feeling more confident after learning something new?38 found it difficult to stay motivated at the beginning?39 learned something mainly for professional reasons?40 enjoyed the social aspect of the experience?41 talks about improving slowly over time?42 mentions being surprised by their own ability?

Texts
A – Laura
I decided to learn how to cook properly last year because I was tired of eating ready-made meals. At first, I found it quite challenging, especially because I made a lot of mistakes. However, I kept practising, and over time I noticed that my skills were improving little by little. Now I feel much more comfortable in the kitchen and even enjoy trying new recipes.

B – Mark
For me, learning graphic design was something I needed for my job. My company expected me to develop these skills, so I didn’t really have a choice. Although I wasn’t very interested at first, I soon realised that I was actually quite good at it. That surprised me, and now I even use these skills for personal projects.

C – Sofia
I joined a photography class because I wanted to meet new people while doing something creative. The classes were fun, and I really enjoyed sharing ideas with others. It was great to be part of a group where everyone supported each other. As a result, I not only improved my photography but also made several good friends.

D – James
I started learning a new language a few months ago. In the beginning, I found it hard to stay motivated because progress seemed very slow. Sometimes I felt like giving up, but I decided to continue. Eventually, I began to understand more, and that gave me the confidence to keep going.

Answer Key
37 D38 D39 B40 C41 A42 B

insert into public.levels_preguntas (id, examen_id, level_id, parte_id, enunciado, creado_en) values (gen_random_uuid(), 'ae0e85e8-3d63-11f1-b2e3-0b27f7b23431', 'ae0e85e8-3d63-11f1-b2e3-0b27f7b23431', 'bd41d80c-bcdd-4ac9-9c06-13c2ab8fab6e', 'Text\nPart 7: Multiple Matching
You are going to read an article in which four people talk about their experiences of working from home. For questions 37–42, choose from the people (A–D). The people may be chosen more than once.

Which person…
37 mentions saving time because of their situation?38 found it difficult to separate work and personal life?39 prefers their current situation to their previous one?40 mentions feeling lonely at times?41 talks about becoming more productive?42 had no choice about the change?

Texts
A – Daniel
When my company decided that everyone had to work from home, I wasn’t very happy about it. I preferred going to the office, but there was nothing I could do. At first, it felt strange, but eventually I got used to it. Now I can see some advantages, although it wasn’t my decision to begin with.

B – Emma
Working from home has made a huge difference to my daily routine. I no longer spend hours travelling to work, which gives me more time to relax or exercise. I feel much happier now than I did before, and I wouldn’t want to go back to my old schedule.

C – Alex
At first, I thought working from home would be easy, but I quickly realised it wasn’t. I found it hard to stop working at the end of the day because everything happened in the same space. It was difficult to create clear boundaries between my job and my personal life.

D – Sara
One thing I didn’t expect was how much I would miss being around other people. Although I can communicate with my colleagues online, it’s not the same as seeing them in person. On the positive side, I’ve noticed that I can concentrate better and get more work done.

Answer Key
37 B38 C39 B40 D41 D42 A
', now());
insert into public.levels_preguntas (id, examen_id, level_id, parte_id, enunciado, creado_en) values (gen_random_uuid(), 'ae0e85e8-3d63-11f1-b2e3-0b27f7b23431', 'ae0e85e8-3d63-11f1-b2e3-0b27f7b23431', 'bd41d80c-bcdd-4ac9-9c06-13c2ab8fab6e', 'Text\nPart 7: Multiple Matching
You are going to read an article in which four people talk about their experiences of practising sport regularly. For questions 37–42, choose from the people (A–D). The people may be chosen more than once.

Which person…
37 says they didn’t enjoy the activity at the beginning?38 mentions that they needed encouragement to continue?39 talks about doing the activity for health reasons?40 says they have made new friends through the activity?41 mentions noticing gradual improvement?42 says they now feel more energetic?

Texts
A – Tom
I started running because my doctor advised me to be more active. At first, I didn’t really like it and found it quite tiring. However, I kept going because I knew it was good for my health. After a few weeks, I began to feel fitter and had much more energy during the day.

B – Lisa
Joining a local yoga class was one of the best decisions I’ve made. Not only have I become more flexible, but I’ve also met some great people. We often talk after class, and sometimes we even meet outside the sessions. It has become both a social and relaxing activity for me.

C – David
When I first started going to the gym, I found it difficult to stay motivated. There were days when I wanted to give up, but my friend encouraged me to keep going. Thanks to that support, I didn’t quit. Over time, I noticed small improvements, which helped me stay focused.

D – Anna
Swimming has always been something I enjoyed, but I never took it seriously until recently. Now I go to the pool three times a week. I’ve seen my technique improve gradually, and I feel more confident in the water. It’s satisfying to see progress, even if it’s slow.

Answer Key
37 A38 C39 A40 B41 D42 A
